page: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v7 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs accompanied by 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per core. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage capabilities on the D16pds_v7 feature 944 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency ephemeral storage alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for persistent managed disks. The bundled NVMe volume serves high-speed scratch space demands without incurring separate network-attached storage latency for temporary files, swap space, or caching tiers.

From an efficiency perspective, the ARM64 platform offers strong performance-per-watt and cost efficiency relative to traditional x86 hardware classes for multi-threaded workloads, though it requires ARM-compatible software stacks. Given the 16 dedicated cores, balanced memory footprint, and fast local NVMe disk, the D16pds_v7 is suited for containerized applications, web application backends, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed databases requiring rapid local caching.
